notes_list.title: Conformational Analysis — Cyclohexane
notes_list.basic_overview: Cyclohexane adopts nonplanar conformations; chair is strongly preferred because it minimizes torsional and angle strain.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Chair conformations have axial and equatorial positions. Ring flip converts axial↔equatorial while retaining up/down orientation. Bulky groups generally prefer equatorial positions.
notes_list.examples: Methylcyclohexane is more stable with methyl equatorial. For disubstituted cyclohexanes, determine whether both substituents can be equatorial in one chair.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Equilibrium between chairs is temperature-dependent but normally rapid at room temperature for ordinary cyclohexanes.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: 1. Draw chair. 2. Mark axial positions alternating up/down. 3. Convert substituent up/down to axial/equatorial. 4. Ring flip without changing up/down. 5. Compare A-values qualitatively.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Axial penalty is often discussed using A-values; disubstituted conformers can be compared by summing substituent penalties as an approximation.
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: High-yield for stereochemical stability and E2 reactions on cyclohexanes.
notes_list.common_traps: Ring flip does not convert cis to trans. It only exchanges axial and equatorial positions.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
